correctness_confidence.basis: Verified 18 zero-sorry Lean 4.35.0 theorems with 0 Classical.choice and exact Q/Z certificate verification across 16 canonical test vectors and 60 adversarial red-team attacks.

novelty.basis: First standalone zero-dependency formalization and certified exact verification framework for Lin et al.'s asymptotic (1-epsilon)-MMS theorem, bridging fair division theory with machine-checked proofs.

reproducibility.basis: Fully reproducible through standalone Lean 4 code, deterministic Python verifiers, and 39 SHA-256 tracked verification artifacts running end-to-end without external dependencies.

rigor.basis: Immaculate mathematical and computational rigor, employing exact rational arithmetic exclusively, strict JSON typing, and exhaustive checks of primal-dual invariants, cyclic compression, and M'' sharing.

significance.basis: Resolves central algorithmic and fair-division verification challenges by establishing absolute computational guarantees for asymptotic maximin share allocations in polynomial bundle comparisons.

strengths: Zero-sorry, zero-Classical.choice formalization of all 18 core theorems in Lean 4.35.0.
Strict zero-floating-point Q/Z arithmetic verifier ensuring absolute precision and immunity to floating-point drift.
Comprehensive adversarial red-team suite demonstrating 60/60 successful rejections across 5 distinct attack categories.
Complete end-to-end reproducibility with SHA-256 manifest verification across 39 tracked artifacts.
strong_novelty_candidates: First machine-checked formalization and exact certificate verifier for asymptotic (1-epsilon)-MMS allocations.
summary: This paper presents a rigorous, standalone, zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 formalization and exact Q/Z certificate verifier (MMS-ASYMP-CERT-1.0) for Lin et al.'s asymptotic (1-epsilon)-MMS fair division theory. Covering 18 machine-checked theorems with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice, 16 canonical certificates, and a 60-attack adversarial red-team validation suite, the work establishes bulletproof computational guarantees for asymptotic maximin share allocations.
weaknesses: Scope is restricted to verifying finite algebraic and combinatorial invariants of Lin et al. rather than formalizing asymptotic O(.) LP-solver runtimes inside Lean 4.
